This is a technical dashboard. It tracks the mod's development progress: which monsters are covered, which creature files are mapped to them, and how their THAC0 and attacks per round compare to the game's originals. It is mainly meant for development, but you may find it interesting to see what is done and what is coming. Terms such as creatures.csv or MonsterId refer to the mod's internal data. For the reworked monsters themselves, see the Monster Compendium.

THAC0 / APR: creatures.csv vs documentation

Each row is one creature file (per game when the doc shows a game-specific card), shown as csv → doc and the difference: green when the doc makes the creature stronger, red when weaker (for THAC0, lower is stronger). Bold cells are relevant differences (THAC0 also highlighted):

  • THAC0: more than 3
  • APR: any difference (csv decoded through AttackPerRoundTable; doc includes the fighter level/proficiency bonus and the off-hand attack)

Only those two put a file in the report. A level difference is bold too and can be filtered on, but never puts a file in the report on its own. HP is shown for context and never flagged. A blank cell means the stat is unchanged.

Creature XP follows the AD&D 2e DMG rule, even below the in-game XP; only an adjustment with keepInGameXp keeps the in-game value (kept). Adjustments' old XP was mostly arbitrary, so All files is for reference: the changes, lowered files and conflicts are what to review.

Statuses
formula
an adjustment scored by the 2e DMG formula: Hit Dice plus the Table 32 abilities
kept
an adjustment with keepInGameXp: the in-game XP, whatever the formula says
as base
the adjustment changes nothing the formula reads, so it takes its base creature's XP
book
a file with no adjustment: the base creature's own XP (its Monstrous Manual value, else its in-game XP)
zero
worth no XP: a summon, an explicit xpv 0 or 0 in game

XP proposals: base creatures (124)

A comparison: XP itself is the DMG formula. In-game = the base files' in-game XP (median, range when they differ), 2e = book XP, DMG = the DMG formula with each strength edition (strengthEdition; hover for its breakdown), then the threat system: the melee and ranged duels' rounds (Rm the monster's, Rf the reference's), the threat T and its XP. Values below the in-game XP are marked. Fit: s = 2.116, k = 0.25 (107 samples).

298880in-game total (107 monsters)
3426652e book (+15%)
402700DMG, 2e Str (+35%)
425765DMG, 3e+ Str (+42%)
355540threat (+19%)

Threat measures a monster against a fighter (melee duel) and an archer (ranged duel) of its own level (its Hit Dice value). A duel: the rounds the monster needs to drop him (Rm) against the rounds he needs to drop it (Rf); their ratio Rf ÷ Rm is about 1 for an even fight. T = melee0.75 × ranged0.25 (× 1.2 invisible at will, × 1.1 per declared ability). Threat XP = Table 31 × s × Tk, s and k fitted by npm run fit-threat on the base creatures with a book and an in-game XP. HP: 10 per level + 3 Con to 9, then +3. AC: 10 at 1-2, plate (3) around 4, full plate (1) around 6, magic items to -5 at 20; the archer's 4 better. Fighter: Strength 18/50, two d8 swords, specialization; archer: Dexterity +2, specialization, two arrows. Enchantment +1 per 4 levels to +3. THAC0 and saves: the 2e warrior tables.
